title: Give the control panel an ssh key it can use on VM 106 (palworld-server)
verify: pct exec 111 -- ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes aedefruscio@192.168.1.106 true

files.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# 1. Ensure the panel has a key in container 111.
pct exec 111 -- sh -c 'test -f /root/.ssh/id_ed25519 || ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -N "" -f /root/.ssh/id_ed25519'

# 2. Capture the panel's public key.
KEY="$(pct exec 111 -- cat /root/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub)"
[ -n "$KEY" ] || { echo 'FAILED: no public key in 111'; exit 1; }

# 3. Read VM 106's real ed25519 host key through the guest agent (not the network).
HOSTKEY="$(qm guest exec 106 -- cat /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub | sed -n 's/.*"out-data":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')"
[ -n "$HOSTKEY" ] || { echo 'FAILED: could not read host key from VM 106'; exit 1; }

# 4. Replace any stale known_hosts entry for 192.168.1.106 in container 111 with the real key.
pct exec 111 -- sh -c "ssh-keygen -R 192.168.1.106 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; printf '%s %s\n' '192.168.1.106' '$HOSTKEY' >> /root/.ssh/known_hosts"

# 5. Back up and repair authorized_keys on VM 106: drop blank lines, dedupe, ensure panel key present exactly once.
qm guest exec 106 -- sh -c "cp -a /home/aedefruscio/.ssh/authorized_keys /home/aedefruscio/.ssh/authorized_keys.bak.\$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S); awk 'NF' /home/aedefruscio/.ssh/authorized_keys | sort -u > /tmp/ak && mv /tmp/ak /home/aedefruscio/.ssh/authorized_keys; grep -Fq '$KEY' /home/aedefruscio/.ssh/authorized_keys || printf '%s\n' '$KEY' >> /home/aedefruscio/.ssh/authorized_keys"

# 6. Test the connection from inside container 111 with strict host-key checking.
pct exec 111 -- ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes aedefruscio@192.168.1.106 true
